activity.notes: Eannatum is securely attested by contemporary Lagash inscriptions and the Stele of the Vultures as ruler of Lagash. Absolute Early Dynastic chronology is not exact: the Louvre dates the Eannatum stele broadly to 2450-2425 BCE, while modern scholarship stresses that the exact length and internal chronology of his reign cannot be reconstructed with certainty. ATLAS therefore uses c.2450-c.2425 BCE only as an approximate reign bracket, not as exact accession and death years.

sources.title: Stèle des vautours — Musée du Louvre
sources.citation_text: The Louvre identifies the Stele of the Vultures as Eannatum's victory monument, calls Eannatum king of Lagash, and dates the monument to the Early Dynastic IIIb period around 2450-2425 BCE.

sources.title: Ensiship and Lugalship of Lagash in the late Early Dynastic Period III — Tohru Maeda
sources.citation_text: Maeda's study of Lagash royal titulature explains the ensi and lugal terminology for rulers including Eannatum and supports modeling him as the ruler of Lagash while keeping titulature historically precise.
